That experience gives the patterns something to connect to. While reading, you can revisit earlier work and consider where a pattern—or a combination of patterns—might have helped.

For me, that is the “Ah!” moment: recognizing how an idea in the book could apply to a problem I had already encountered. It makes an abstract description feel practical.

There is also a useful question to keep beside that recognition: would the pattern have made the design clearer, or would it have introduced complexity the problem did not need? Having a name for a solution is useful; understanding when it earns its place is the more interesting challenge.
